answer.reason: Table 1 of the New Jersey Electricity Profile splits net generation between 'Electric generators' and 'IPP & CHP.' New Jersey's traditional utilities own almost no generating capacity, so nearly all of the state's roughly 60 million MWh of annual net generation comes from independent power producers and combined heat and power plants. This is confirmed by the fact that the two candidate figures are complementary: 59,911,662 + 263,583 = 60,175,245 MWh, which matches New Jersey's total net generation. Therefore 59,911,662 MWh is the IPP & CHP subtotal and 263,583 MWh is the much smaller electric generators subtotal. This agrees with the user's check of the cited source, so the draft answer B is corrected to A.
